This page is a draft, so `quarto preview` shows it but the published site never includes it. Open `posts/style-guide/index.qmd` next to this page to see the source for everything below.

## Maths

Inline: $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n^{-s}$. Display, numbered so you can refer to it as @eq-gauss:

$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} \dd x = \sqrt{\pi}
$$ {#eq-gauss}

Hover any display equation to get a **Copy TeX** button. Site-wide macros (defined in `theme/katex-macros.html`) include `\N \Z \Q \R \C \F`, `\abs{x}`, `\norm{v}`, `\floor{x}`, `\set{\dots}`, `\inner{u}{v}`, `\dd`:
$$
\abs{x} \le \norm{v}, \qquad \floor{\pi} = 3, \qquad \set{n \in \Z : n > 0} = \N.
$$

Aligned equations:
$$
\begin{aligned}
(a+b)^2 &= a^2 + 2ab + b^2 \\
        &\ge 4ab.
\end{aligned}
$$

## Theorem-like environments

Each type gets its own counter, and any of them can be cross-referenced: @thm-demo, @lem-demo, @def-demo.

::: {#thm-demo}
## Optional name
Theorems, lemmas (`#lem-`), corollaries (`#cor-`), propositions (`#prp-`), and conjectures (`#cnj-`) are set in italics with a marigold rule.
:::

::: {#lem-demo}
A lemma.
:::

::: {#def-demo}
## Definition style
Definitions (`#def-`), examples (`#exm-`), and exercises (`#exr-`) are set upright.
:::

::: {#cnj-demo}
Conjectures get a dashed rule.
:::

::: {.proof}
Proofs end with a filled square. Click the word **Proof** to fold one away.
:::

::: {.proof collapse="true"}
Add `collapse="true"` and the proof starts folded, so readers can try it themselves first.
:::

::: {#exr-demo}
Show that $n^2 + n$ is always even.
:::

::: {.solution}
Solutions start folded. $n^2 + n = n(n+1)$, and one of two consecutive integers is even. (Use `collapse="false"` to show one open.)
:::

::: {.remark}
Remarks are quieter.
:::

To fold every proof in a post, put `fold-proofs: true` in its front matter. Readers can always flip them all with **Hide all proofs** under the contents list, or the <kbd>p</kbd> key.

Every definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary and conjecture you write also appears on the **Theorems** page automatically, searchable, with a link back to the post.

## Commutative diagrams

KaTeX understands the `CD` environment from `amscd`. Keep `\begin{CD}` on the same line as the opening `$$` and `\end{CD}` on the same line as the closing one (otherwise Pandoc treats it as raw LaTeX):

$$\begin{CD}
A @>{f}>> B \\
@V{g}VV @VV{h}V \\
C @>>{k}> D
\end{CD}$$

Arrows are `@>>>` (right), `@<<<` (left), `@VVV` (down), `@AAA` (up) and `@=` (equals), with labels between the symbols: `@>{f}>>` puts $f$ above. For anything fancier (curved or diagonal arrows), draw it as an SVG and include it as an image.

## Series

Give posts the same `series:` in their front matter and they're linked together:

```yaml
series: "Galois theory from scratch"
```

Each part gets a box under the title listing every part (in date order), a "Next in the series" link at the bottom, and the series gets its own card on the Topics page.

## Revised dates

If you change a post substantially after publishing it, add `date-modified: 2026-12-01` to the front matter. It shows as "Revised" next to the original date.

## Share images

Every post gets its own preview image (title, categories and a patch of the prime spiral) when the site is published, so links look good in Discord, iMessage and so on. To use your own picture, add `image: my-picture.png` to the front matter.

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
## Note
Use `callout-note`, `callout-tip`, `callout-warning`, `callout-important`, `callout-caution`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## A collapsible hint (click me)
Add `collapse="true"` to hide a hint or a spoiler until the reader asks for it.
:::

## Sidenotes and margin content

Footnotes become sidenotes on wide screens.^[Like this one. On phones they appear at the bottom.] You can also put anything in the margin:

::: {.column-margin}
A margin note, written with `::: {.column-margin}`. Figures can go here too.
:::

## Code

```python
def sieve(n):
    is_prime = [True] * (n + 1)
    is_prime[0:2] = [False, False]
    for p in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if is_prime[p]:
            is_prime[p*p::p] = [False] * len(is_prime[p*p::p])
    return [p for p, ok in enumerate(is_prime) if ok]
```

## Linking to a theorem in another post

Link to its label with empty link text, and the link names itself ("Theorem 1 (Euclid)"). Hovering it shows the statement:

```markdown
There are infinitely many primes ([](../infinitely-many-primes/#thm-euclid)).
```

That renders as: there are infinitely many primes ([](../infinitely-many-primes/#thm-euclid)). Any link from one post, note or problem to another also adds a "Referenced by" entry at the bottom of the page it points to.

## Interactive graphs

A graph with sliders, drawn by the site itself:

```markdown
{{</* plot "sin(a*x) / x; cos(b*x)" a=1..4 b=0.5..2 x=-10..10 caption="Drag the sliders" */>}}
```

{{< plot "sin(a*x) / x; cos(b*x)" a=1..4 b=0.5..2 x=-10..10 caption="Drag the sliders" >}}

Separate several functions with `;`. Any single letter other than `x` and `y` becomes a slider (`a=1..4`, or `a=0..1..0.05` to set the step). `x=` and `y=` fix the axes; without `y=` the graph scales itself. You can write `2x`, `x^2`, `sqrt`, `ln`, `exp`, `abs`, `pi` and the trig functions.

Saved graphs from elsewhere work too: `{{</* desmos ID */>}}` (the ID is the end of the graph's share link) and `{{</* geogebra ID */>}}`. In the PDF version these become a note pointing to the web page.

## Interactive widgets (Observable JS, no install needed)

```{ojs}
//| echo: true
viewof k = Inputs.range([1, 20], {value: 6, step: 1, label: "k"})
md`$${k}! = ${d3.range(1, k + 1).reduce((a, b) => a * b, 1).toLocaleString()}$`
```
